record.original_question: Extend Paige's analysis of the Lanczos algorithm to the block Lanczos algorithm. The exact analysis will depend on the use of an orthogonalization scheme used within blocks, so either specify certain assumptions on the accuracy of the scheme, or analyze a standard ``good'' algorithm.

evidence.quote: Extend Paige's analysis of the Lanczos algorithm \cite{paige_76,paige_80} to the block Lanczos algorithm. The exact analysis will depend on the use of an orthogonalization scheme used within blocks, so either specify certain assumptions on the accuracy of the scheme, or analyze a standard ``good'' algorithm.

artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 paper "On finite precision block Lanczos computations" (arXiv:2507.16484, BIT Numerical Mathematics) extends Paige/Greenbaum-type analysis to the block Lanczos algorithm, generalizing the backward-error/continuation interpretation in terms of a nearby larger model matrix and deriving sufficient conditions on the intra-block orthogonalization for the perturbations to remain small. However, the authors note that whereas in the single-vector case these conditions can always be met, in the block case it remains open whether they can always be satisfied, so the program is only partially completed.

status_evidence.title: On finite precision block Lanczos computations
status_evidence.snippet: Extends Paige-type analysis to block Lanczos: computed block tridiagonal matrix interpreted as arising from exact block Lanczos applied to a larger model matrix; sufficient conditions on perturbations; open whether they can always be satisfied in the block case.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extension of Paige's finite-precision analysis to the block Lanczos algorithm exists, but key questions remain open.

status_evidence.title: On finite precision block Lanczos computations | BIT Numerical Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Published version in BIT addressing finite precision behavior of block Lanczos.
status_evidence.claim: Recent journal publication addresses (partially) the extension problem.

$$ A X_k = X_{k-1} B_{k-1}^T + X_k M_k + X_{k+1} B_k, $$
where $M_k = X_k^T A X_k$ and $X_{k+1} B_k$ is obtained by orthogonalizing $A X_k - X_{k-1} B_{k-1}^T - X_k M_k$ against $X_k$ (with $X_0 := 0$, $B_0 := 0$) and then performing an intra-block QR-type orthogonalization to produce $X_{k+1}$ with orthonormal columns and the upper-triangular factor $B_k$. After $k$ steps, the computed block tridiagonal matrix
$$ T_k = \begin{pmatrix} M_1 & B_1^T & & \\ B_1 & M_2 & B_2^T & \\ & B_2 & \ddots & \ddots \\ & & \ddots & M_k \end{pmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{kb \times kb} $$
yields approximate eigenvalues (Ritz values) of $A$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item the residual of the block three-term recurrence;
\item the loss of orthogonality $\|\hat{X}_j^T \hat{X}_k\|$ both within blocks and between blocks;
\item the size and structure of the perturbations needed so that the computed $T_k$ may be interpreted as arising from an exact block Lanczos process applied to a nearby larger symmetric matrix; and
\item the implications for the accuracy of the computed Ritz values as approximations to eigenvalues of $A$.
